shortDescription: FPA said on Tuesday it intended to support activist investor Oasis' nominees for Vail Resorts NYSE:MTN amid a proxy battle with the mountain resort operator.

children: FPA said on Tuesday it intended to support activist investor Oasis' nominees for Vail Resorts
amid a proxy battle with the mountain resort operator.

FPA, which holds a 3.7% stake in Vail, said the ski resort's financial performance had fallen well short of its potential from the pre-COVID period and described it as "stagnant while other high-end leisure assets or activities have experienced robust growth"
It said that Oasis nominees, former CEO of Walt Disney
Robert Chapek and investor M. Ashton Hudson, will bring relevant expertise, fresh perspectives and independent accountability to Vail's board

Oasis management urged Vail shareholders earlier this week to elect its two director nominees at the company's upcoming shareholder meeting on December 14, after it had reduced its nominees to two from four
"Given the board's record, it is reasonable and necessary to select directors who originate from outside the board's echo chamber," said Brian Selmo, partner at FPA
Vail owns mountain resorts and ski areas including in Utah, Colorado and the northeastern US
Last month, Vail secured support for its nominees from Baron Capital, its largest shareholder which owns about 18% of the company
Vail did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment
